study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain charts for the human lifespan

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study explicitly states its objective to create brain charts to benchmark individual variation in brain morphology and to quantify atypicality in neurological and psychiatric disorders.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here we assemble an interactive open resource to benchmark brain morphology derived from any current or future sample of MRI data... In summary, brain charts are an essential step towards robust quantification of individual variation benchmarked to normative trajectories...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study aggregates data from over 100 primary studies. It describes the aggregation process, the inclusion of healthy controls (reference cohort), and specifies quality control procedures (Euler index, expert visual curation). It reports the final sample size (123,984 scans).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans, across more than 100 primary studies... image quality control, which used a combination of expert visual curation and automated metrics of image quality (Supplementary Information 2)

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The GAMLSS models explicitly account for age (non-linear trajectories) and are stratified by sex. Study/site effects are modelled as random effects to handle batch effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Normative brain-volume trajectories were estimated using GAMLSS, accounting for site- and study-specific batch effects, and stratified by sex

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data sources (over 100 primary studies) are described and listed in Supplementary Information 19 and tables.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: See Supplementary Information 19 for details on all primary studies contributing to the reference dataset, including multiple publicly available open MRI datasets

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Acquisition parameters for the aggregated datasets are detailed in Supplementary Tables 1.1-1.8.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Supplementary Tables 1.1-1.8 present details on acquisition, processing and demographics of the dataset

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The study specifies that most scans (~95%) were processed with FreeSurfer. It also discusses the versions used and quality control.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: scans processed by FreeSurfer (~95% of the reference dataset)... Supplementary Tables 1.1-1.8 present details on acquisition, processing...

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study used cross-validation (leave-one-study-out) and bootstrap resampling to validate the models.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The reliability of the models was assessed and endorsed by cross-validation and bootstrap resampling procedures (Supplementary Information 3).
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Methods, Model generation and specification

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The model was tested on external datasets not included in the reference model, such as the '10k-in-a-day' dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: We also compared the results of the lifespan model to an MRI dataset (10k-in-a-day) that could not be incorporated into the reference dataset

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study uses Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS). It specifies the model terms (fractional polynomials) and software (R).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: We created brain charts for the human lifespan using generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS)...

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance was assessed using BIC for distribution selection, Q-Q plots, and worm plots (Detrended transformed Owen's plots).
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Detrended transformed Owen's plots of the ordered centile residuals clearly showed that the confidence intervals crossed the zero line, indicating normally distributed residuals

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: The study used bootstrapping stratified by study and sex, preserving the characteristics. Sample sizes and demographics are detailed.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: The bootstrap replicates were stratified by study and sex, which maintains the relative proportions of the original datasets.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Code and models are openly available.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: We have provided an interactive tool (www.brainchart.io) and made our code and models openly available (https://github.com/brainchart/Lifespan).

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The study aggregated clinical cohorts from existing studies. It references the original studies for detailed criteria and reports sample sizes for each condition.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: See Supplementary Information 19 for details on all primary studies... Patient eligibility and diagnostic criteria are described... (e.g., DSM-5, ICD-10, clinical interviews)

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: The study analysed some covariates like birth weight and gestational age in relation to centile scores, and looked at diagnostic progression (MCI to AD). However, systematic control for medication or symptom severity across all aggregated clinical groups was not the primary focus of the main broad comparisons.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: average centile scores across global tissues were related to two metrics of premature birth... individuals who changed diagnostic categories... showed small but significant increases in within-subject variability

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical data sources are the same as the reference sources (many studies included both cases and controls) and are fully described.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Supplementary Information 19 for details on all primary studies

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes and demographics for clinical groups are reported in Supplementary Tables.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Demographics for each cross-sectional sample... are detailed in Supplementary Table 1.2-1.8

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Diagnostic categories are the main measure. Some dimensional measures like fluid intelligence were also analysed in subsets.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: Clinical groups were aggregated by categorical diagnosis... or for endorsement of symptomatology

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The study extensively interprets deviation scores (centiles and CMD) in the context of disorders, discussing the direction and magnitude of differences.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Relative to the control group (CN), there were highly significant differences in centile scores across large (N > 500) groups of cases... Alzheimer's disease showed the greatest overall difference...
